newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's parliament passes law on opposition gains.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's parliament passes law on opposition gains.

text.p: The Serbian parliament passed a special law on Tuesday reinstating in principle opposition victories in local elections last November.

President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialists had annulled opposition gains in 14 towns and cities on grounds of unspecified "irregularities", prompting months of mass protests and an international outcry.
The Serbian deputies voted 128 in favour of the bill, one abstained and one refrained, the speaker of the parliament said.

The deputies then moved on to vote on seven amendments to the bill, including those submited by the opposition to restore their victory in Novi Beograd and Mladenovac municipalities which were not listed in an OSCE report.

The ruling Socialists had annulled November's opposition victories in 14 cities including Belgrade on grounds of "irregularities". The action prompted three months of huge protests and attracted an international outcry.
A week ago president Slobodan Milosevic suddenly announced he was asking parliament to approve a bill recognising the opposition gains.
